_demand_record.detail: RE-ANCHOR (this is the flagship fix). OLD model: Monaco Heliport throughput 79,000 x 2% = 1,580/yr -> effectively zero on one of the richest marine corridors on earth. The 79,000 is NOT a mass pool to take 2% of; it is ALREADY the premium Nice-Airport<->Monaco transfer pool (every one of these pax pays ~EUR 195/seat to fly today). The correct addressable anchor is therefore the FULL 79,000 transfer pool (no further haircut), with clear UPSIDE from diverting a share of Nice Airport's 15.23M annual ground-transfer flow to a sub-heli-priced fast sea shuttle. 79,000 counts both directions; distinc

_demand_record.detail: Destination pool = ~1.6M tourists/yr to the Golfe de Saint-Tropez (Communaute de communes Golfe de Saint-Tropez). Saint-Tropez is mainland (also road-accessible, hence a premium SHARE not a near-full pool), so a 2% premium-willing share is applied = 32,000 one-way/yr (consistent with the prior anchor & payload). Upper-bound context: Saint-Tropez town records ~17.7M visitor-FOOTFALL/yr -- deliberately NOT used as the base. NOTE: this pool is shared with the Nice->Saint-Tropez corridor below; do not double-count the 1.6M.

_demand_record.detail: RAIL: Gare de Cannes 5,622,000 voyageurs (2024) used as the destination-end rail touchpoint on the Nice<->Cannes axis (Nice-Ville itself is 12,131,000 but that spreads over many O-Ds, so Cannes is the more conservative corridor proxy). ROAD: A8 Nice-Cannes is among France's most congested interurban segments (adds materially on top). 4% premium-willing haircut for a fast gridlock-skipping sea shuttle. NOTE: throughput counts both directions / all O-Ds at Cannes, so the figure over-attributes somewhat to this one corridor; the modest 4% absorbs that.

RAIL: Gare d'Antibes 3,414,872 voyageurs (2024) as the origin-end rail touchpoint on the Antibes<->Cannes/Golfe-Juan axis. ROAD: coastal RD6007 + A8 congested in season. 4% premium-willing haircut. Same both-directions/all-O-D caveat as the other rail-anchored corridors.

_demand_record.detail: No rail on the Amalfi Coast; substitution is road (SS163) + the already-busy in-season ferry. POOL = Amalfi Coast total visitors ~5,000,000/yr (US News; '5 million people visit Amalfi every year'). 4% premium-willing haircut for travelers who would pay for a fast gridlock-skipping shuttle on the Positano<->Amalfi axis = ~200,000 one-way/yr. NOTE: 5M is the whole-coast figure; the Positano<->Amalfi leg is a core but partial segment of it, so the 4% blends segment-share AND premium-capture. Conservative regional proxy (overnight-only is far smaller at 564,981 across 13 towns, 2023). Flagged.

RAIL: EAV Circumvesuviana Napoli-Sorrento line carried ~5,000,000 passengers/yr (2023; ~15,000/day, peaks >40,000) -- the dominant Naples<->Sorrento ground flow; the whole Circumvesuviana network does ~38M journeys/yr. ROAD: SS145 Sorrentina is chronically saturated in season. POOL = ~5,000,000 rail riders (conservative; road adds on top). 4% premium-willing haircut for a fast gridlock-skipping sea shuttle (a seasonal Naples-Sorrento fast ferry already exists) = ~200,000 one-way/yr. NOTE: rail ridership counts both directions / all O-Ds on the line; the 4% absorbs over-attribution. Flagged.
